**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) — Rule T4C, ¶ 4(a) (p0016).**

**Issue.** The term provision creates a one-year Initial Term that auto-renews for successive 1-year terms, and expressly bars *either* party from terminating during the Initial Term. AP therefore has no convenience exit at all in a term that rolls indefinitely past 12 months — a missing-behaviour deviation from our preferred position (30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees). Separately, the symmetry cuts against us: Kubient can walk away "for any reason" on 90 days' notice at *any* point after the Initial Term, rather than only at the end of a committed term.

**Redline (validated, preferred level).** Replaced the two lock-in sentences with:
- an AP convenience right, exercisable at any time (including during the Initial Term), on 30 days' written notice, with refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination fee or penalty; and
- a Kubient convenience right limited to termination effective at the end of the then-current Term on not less than 90 days' notice.

**Note for negotiation.** I deliberately left intact the retained sentence giving Kubient "all fees generated during the termination period," since in this revenue-share auction context those are fees actually earned on impressions run during the notice window, not a penalty. If Kubient tries to read that sentence as an early-termination charge triggered by our new 30-day right, it should be tightened to "fees actually generated" — worth watching in the redline exchange. The comment offers the 60–90 day fallback if Kubient needs a longer runway.
